clue.text: Swimmer with partner often seen in newspaper

definitions.text: Swimmer with partner often seen in newspaper

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
and joins things, as with does
chips accompany the fish, and the pair was traditionally wrapped in newspaper

explanation.surface: A swimmer and their partner keep appearing in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the British takeaway, long sold wrapped in old newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered fish served with chips is the classic British takeaway, once wrapped in newsprint.

clue.text: Helter-Skelter etc Fab Four originally based round a French song

definitions.note: the definition names examples of rides, standing for the place that has them

indicators.note: the two initials sit round the French article, one on each side
originally points to the opening letter of each of Fab and Four

parts.note: the first letters of Fab and Four
UN is French for a
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: The Beatles' Helter Skelter, recast as a French chanson built around the Fab Four.
explanation.walkthrough: Helter Skelter is a Beatles song, so the Fab Four look like part of the topic; here a helter-skelter is the spiral slide at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A helter-skelter is a spiral fairground slide, one of the rides found at an amusement fair.

clue.text: Creep turned on that woman after close of business

indicators.note: the lit-and-her part comes after the closing letter
the close of a word is its final letter, here of business

parts.note: its closing letter is S
a lamp that has been turned on is lit
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A creep's advances to a woman after office hours are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a noun for an unpleasant man but is the verb to move stealthily.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide along stealthily like a snake, a way of creeping.

clue.text: Food social worker needed by 13:01

parts.note: ants are social insects and workers in the colony
1.01 pm is one past one, written as I PAST I

explanation.surface: A care worker needs lunch at one minute past one.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker is an ant in crosswords; 13:01 on the clock is one past one, with each one as the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters such as cured meats and olives, served before the main dishes.

clue.text: Trick using quarter that's increased times ten initially

indicators.note: the opening letter, a Roman numeral fifty, is multiplied by ten to give the numeral for five hundred

parts.note: a lodge is lodgings, quarters to live in

explanation.surface: A sleight of hand that inflates a quarter tenfold.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals L is 50 and D is 500, so raising the first letter tenfold swaps L for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning trick or ruse used to evade something.

clue.text: Try and eat earlier

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it
ago means earlier, in the past

explanation.surface: An instruction to taste the food and to eat beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is the idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: Joke and poke one's tongue

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a jab is a quick poke
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A child jokes and then pokes out their tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like the body part being poked out, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the language spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: These married sisters

definitions.meaning: a sister's husband becomes a relative by marriage

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a description of sisters who are married; it means the men who wed them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister's husband is your relative by marriage, so the men who wed the sisters gain that family title.

clue.text: Homer apt, conceivably, to say it's not rocket surgery?

definitions.meaning: the letters of homer apt jumbled make a figure of speech, so this is that figure mixed up

definitions.text: to say it's not rocket surgery?
definitions.meaning: rocket science and brain surgery are two idioms jammed together

explanation.walkthrough: Homer seems the poet, but his letters with apt, conceivably rearranged, spell a figure of speech in muddled form; the second half gives an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Blending two clichés, as in 'rocket surgery', combines incompatible images in one phrase.

clue.text: Raise hell as youngest to tour exotic city

indicators.note: the youngest goes all round the city, enclosing it

parts.note: the runt is the smallest, often last-born, of a litter
Rio de Janeiro, the glamorous Brazilian city

explanation.surface: The youngest child behaves wildly on a trip to a glamorous foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is the idiom for behaving wildly and without restraint.

clue.text: 'Un peu de soda, vin, cidre' — French king's favourite

indicators.note: French for 'a little of', so only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across soda, vin and cidre

explanation.surface: A French menu offering a little soda, wine and cider.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is itself the signal: a little of the words. Leonardo spent his last years in France as a favourite of King Francis I.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo was invited to France by Francis I, who honoured and favoured the painter at Amboise.

clue.text: Change seat and dance in place of drinking

indicators.note: the letters of seat are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A rearrangement of chairs for a dance in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place of drinking' suggests a bar, but the drink is tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving tea and light refreshments is a spot where people drink.

clue.text: Scoffed after label back-to-front becomes issue

indicators.note: the eating word comes after the label
back-to-front means the word for label is read from its end

parts.note: a name is a label for something
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed is ate

explanation.surface: Eating something whose label was the wrong way round turns into a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun meaning problem, but it is the verb to flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or originate from a source, as a sound or smell does.

clue.text: Nought in English reading, writing and arithmetic — must be a mistake!

indicators.note: the nought is placed in among the other letters

parts.note: the three Rs of basic education
nought, zero, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Scoring zero in English and the basics is surely an error of marking.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, each spelt with an R sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something done wrongly.

clue.text: Say I'm up, conscious, oddly attending maiden conference

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and every other odd letter of the words are kept

parts.note: its odd-placed letters, read across all the words
in cricket a maiden over is recorded as M

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they are awake and alert at a meeting with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A symposium is a formal meeting where experts discuss a topic.

clue.text: Required staff prosecutor to crush Conservative

indicators.note: in a down answer the prosecutor sits on top of the Conservative, pressing down on it

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Staff and a prosecutor are needed to defeat a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is a US district attorney; Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mandatory is compulsory, demanded by a rule or law.

clue.text: Line-up of clones tie for corruption

indicators.note: corruption of the words is a garbling of their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police line-up of identical clones, linked by corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a chosen group, such as a team's lineup picked for a match.

clue.text: No parking on drain, one hears!

definitions.note: a noun phrase read as 'one (thing) that hears', the organ of hearing

indicators.note: no parking says the parking letter is removed
the parking letter is the one sitting on, at the head of, the drain word

parts.note: a plughole is the drain in a sink or bath

explanation.surface: A No Parking sign over a drain, and the exclamation 'hear hear'.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the parking sign; 'one hears' means a thing one hears with.
explanation.definitionFit: Lughole is British slang for the ear, the organ used for hearing.

clue.text: Playwright's payment from broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the words are spoken, so their sound counts

parts.note: a cheque of someone, read aloud

explanation.surface: A dramatist's fee coming from a radio production.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'cheque off' resembles the Russian name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a Russian dramatist, author of The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard.

clue.text: River creature, rat, finally put to flight

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of rat

parts.note: its final letter is T
to rout an enemy is to drive them away in disorder

explanation.surface: A water rat, at last, chased away by the river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the river creature, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish found in rivers and streams.

clue.text: Poet's last revolutionary verse expert finds explosive

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word poet, ignoring the possessive ending

parts.note: the word poet itself, the 's meaning 'is' and reading as poet's last letter

indicators.note: revolutionary means the verse and expert words are turned round

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A radical poet's ode is found to be dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon carrying a warhead.

clue.text: Madonna's no time for loud, arty rocking

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters into a new order
no time says the time letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The pop singer Madonna has no time for loud, arty rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Madonna looks like the pop star, but the definition is the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin Mary is called the Madonna in Christian art and devotion.

clue.text: Coated in just egg, uncooked round pieces of chicken

indicators.note: round means the run of letters is turned the other way
the answer is coated by, and so lies within, the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters sits across just, egg and uncooked

explanation.surface: A recipe: chicken pieces coated in raw egg and rolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken nuggets are small coated, fried pieces of chicken meat.

clue.text: Who could lure Your Highness north?

parts.note: sire is a form of address to a king

explanation.surface: A question about who could tempt a monarch to travel north.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Sirens' singing lured sailors to wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman; in myth the Sirens enticed sailors onto rocks.

clue.text: Publish splash that's delivered from on high

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the thing delivered, rather than the act

parts.note: to air views is to make them public
a drop is a small splash of liquid

explanation.surface: A newspaper scoop that seems handed down by divine authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splash' suggests a front-page story, but here it is a drop of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop is a load of supplies dropped by parachute from an aircraft.

clue.text: One more ace, not hearts, followed by queen

indicators.note: the queen comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player draws another ace, not a heart, then a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, one extra of the same kind.

clue.text: Recipes may use 1 tsp of this, or say a number

definitions.text: Recipes may use 1 tsp of this
definitions.note: a herb measured by the teaspoon

parts.note: taken as written
say introduces an example, as e.g. does
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookbook direction to add a teaspoon of something, or some other amount.
explanation.walkthrough: NO is short for number; 'say' gives EG, short for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a dried Mediterranean herb often added to recipes by the teaspoonful.

clue.text: Sun pin-up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a star, an object in the sky
second meaning: a gorgeous figure, playfully 'heavenly'

explanation.walkthrough: Sun could be the tabloid with its page-three pin-ups; instead each word is one sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A star or planet is a celestial object, and an attractive physique can be jokingly called divine.
